newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to fine Samsung for late filing of AST deal.
newsitem.headline: EU to fine Samsung for late filing of AST deal.

text.p: The European Commission, asserting its power to vet mergers and takeovers throughout the world that affect the EU market, said on Tuesday it may fine Samsung Electronics Co Ltd for being late in filing for EU approval of its control of AST Research Inc.
A Commission source said later that the fine would be a minimum 100,000 European currency units ($113,500) and that it was sure to happen.

The Commission on Tuesday cleared Samsung's offer to buy all the shares in the Californian personal computer maker that it does not already own, but stressed that the deal should have been filed when Samsung acquired control of the company.
The South Korean company and its affiliates already owned a stake of about 46 percent when it announced in April a tender offer for all remaining shares.
"The European Commission authorises the acquisition of AST by Samsung but considers imposing a fine for late filing," the Commission said in a statement.

Under EU merger control law, the acquisition by a company of a controlling stake in another or any other corporate concentrations with a European dimension must be submitted to the Commission for clearance no more than one week after being concluded or publicly announced.
The Commission, the EU's competition watchdog, said Samsung gained control of AST in January 1996.
The final fine will depend on Samsung's reasons for failing to its duty to seek regulatory approval wherever required and on the opinion of a committee of competition experts from the EU's 15 states.
